comments.body:
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Misspelled env var in the fail-loud remediation message — it names a knob the tool never reads**

Line 115 (this file) tells the operator: *"Remediation: keep the FLUTER_SWIFT_PACKAGE_MANAGER=0 job pin …"*. That name is missing a "T" (`FLUTER_SWIFT_PACKAGE_MANAGER` — F-L-U-T-E-R — vs the name the tool actually reads, `FLUTTER_SWIFT_PACKAGE_MANAGER`, F-L-U-T-E-R) and is therefore a **no-op**: the only env override flutter_tools consults for this feature is `FLUTTER_SWIFT_PACKAGE_MANAGER` — verified in the Flutter tool source, `packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/features.dart`:

```dart
const swiftPackageManager = Feature(
  ...
  environmentOverride: 'FLUTTER_SWIFT_PACKAGE_MANAGER',
```

In this diagnostic branch the specific `fail` exits before the generic message on line 123 (which is spelled correctly) is ever printed, so the misspelled name is the **only** remediation the operator sees for the literal gh-180 shape — copy-pasting it into the job env reproduces the same red leg. The same typo is in the header comment, line 22.

The workflow pin itself (build-macos.yml:131) and the test assertion keys are byte-verified correct, so the lane works — but a fail-loud gate's remediation text is its product on the failure path and must name a real knob.

Suggested fix (both occurrences: lines 22 and 115) — replace the 28-char misspelling with the 29-char real name:

```bash
sed -i 's/FLUTER_SWIFT_PACKAGE_MANAGER/FLUTTER_SWIFT_PACKAGE_MANAGER/g' scripts/assert_macos_min_platform.sh
```

Tests keep passing after the fix: AC3/AC4b assert the corrected line-123 generic message (`contains('FLUTTER_SWIFT_PACKAGE_MANAGER')`), and AC3's `contains('minimum platform version')` matches this line's floor text, which the fix doesn't touch.

Lines 15 and 52 (this file) and `test/macos_min_platform_gate_test.dart:21` spell the env var `FLUTER_SWIFT_PACKAGE_MANAGER` (28 chars — missing a "T"); the tool reads `FLUTTER_SWIFT_PACKAGE_MANAGER` (29 chars). The *assertions* in both files use the correct 29-char key, so nothing is behaviorally wrong — but these doc strings are what future readers will copy when reproducing the pin (the same failure mode as the gate script's remediation message). Same one-line sweep fixes all three:

```bash
sed -i 's/FLUTER_SWIFT_PACKAGE_MANAGER/FLUTTER_SWIFT_PACKAGE_MANAGER/g' test/build_macos_spm_lane_guard_test.dart test/macos_min_platform_gate_test.dart
```

comments.author: unknown
comments.body:
💡 **SUGGESTION: Heads-up — the SwiftPM-off knob this lane pins on is slated for removal upstream**

The fix's linchpin is the `FLUTTER_SWIFT_PACKAGE_MANAGER=0` job pin (correctly spelled here — byte-verified against the tool source). Two data points from the Flutter tool, both read this run:

- `packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/features.dart` declares the feature with `warningMessageOnDisable`: *"Enabling Swift Package Manager will be required in a future version of Flutter."* — i.e. the disable path is deprecation-warned.
- Upstream issue https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/193978 ("No longer allow SwiftPM to be disabled globally or per project") tracks removing the flag entirely.

When that lands, the pure-CocoaPods lane decision needs a different mechanism (e.g. pinning the tool version tighter, or migrating the generated package's floor control). Nothing to change in this PR — the gate will fail loud the day the pin stops working, which is exactly its job. Worth a tracking issue so the removal doesn't arrive as a surprise red leg.

comments.body:
## Automated Code Review — APPROVE (with suggestions)

**Summary**: Well-built fix for the gh-180 DMG lane: the `FLUTTER_SWIFT_PACKAGE_MANAGER=0` job pin and the `flutter build macos --config-only` + gate ordering were verified against the actual flutter_tools sources (`features.dart`, `flutter_features_config.dart`, `build_macos.dart`), the new gate script passes its 15 tests on this tree, and `dart analyze`/`dart format` are clean. No blocking issues; two important nits should be fixed.

**Key Issues**:
- ⚠️ IMPORTANT: `scripts/assert_macos_min_platform.sh:115` (and :22) — the fail-loud remediation message names a misspelled env var (`FLUTER_SWIFT_PACKAGE_MANAGER`, 28 chars) that the tool never reads; it is the only remediation printed for the literal gh-180 shape.
- ⚠️ IMPORTANT: `test/macos_min_platform_gate_test.dart:271` — the "committed tree passes the gate" test reads the live working tree, so it goes red on macOS dev checkouts where Flutter 3.47's default SwiftPM migration has run (contradicts the PR's "dev machines unaffected" note).
- 💡 SUGGESTION: same 28-char misspelling in test comments/titles (`build_macos_spm_lane_guard_test.dart:15,52`, `macos_min_platform_gate_test.dart:21`).
- 💡 SUGGESTION: upstream is moving to remove the SwiftPM disable path (`warningMessageOnDisable` in `features.dart`; flutter/flutter#193978) — the pure-CocoaPods lane pin has a limited shelf life; worth a tracking note.

**Next Steps**:
1. Fix the misspelled env var in the gate script (sed one-liner in the inline comment; tests keep passing).
2. Scope the real-repo-state gate test to committed state or skip when local SwiftPM state exists.
3. Sweep the 28-char misspelling from the two test files' comments/titles.
